title: registry is the iteration domain
docstring: An enforcement check whose finding-emitting loop iterates an opt-in registry examines only the entries somebody volunteered. When that registry is empty in the tree, the check reports a clean verdict over a population it never looked at, and that verdict is indistinguishable from one earned by inspection. A registry must be a FILTER applied to an independently derived population, never the population itself: a check that cannot state how many candidates it examined has not examined any.
pattern: A deterministic check loads a tracked registry file and its only finding-emitting loop iterates that registry. Every candidate the check exists to judge is invisible unless somebody first volunteered it, so an empty registry yields a pass with a denominator of zero while the condition it guards is live elsewhere in the tree. The two shapes are told apart by structure alone: a registry that is the iteration target, versus a registry consulted as membership inside a loop over a derived population.
fix_action: Walk every program that reads a tracked registry file. Parse it and locate each loop that can append a finding. When the loop's iteration target resolves to the registry rather than to a derived population, refuse, naming the loop line and the registry path. Require the verdict to state two denominators — candidates examined, and registry rows applied — and refuse a verdict that states neither. Apply the same refusal when the registry parses to zero rows while candidates exist, since that is the state in which the check is inert and reads as clean.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a (v1.11.33). 29 tracked registry JSON files scanned under tools/ci and programs/. 3 have every collection empty. Structural discrimination over those 3: gate_red_since.json ('acknowledged', 0 rows) is the iteration domain of a finding-emitting `for row in ledger` at gate_red_since_check.py:194 -> THE DEFECT; tool_diagnostic_id_acceptance.json ('accepted', 0 rows) is consulted inside `for ... in enumerate(entries)` -> correct filter; tracked_symlink_target_baseline.json ('known', 0 rows) has no finding-emitting loop over it -> correct filter. 1 finding, 2 correctly not flagged, 0 false positives. Beside it: the same lane measured the hygiene suite on that commit at 'declared 85 | ran 85 | decided 75 | PASS 67 | FAIL 8 | NOT_CHECKED 10' — 8 live reds, 0 acknowledgement rows, and gate_red_since_check exits '[PASS] every red is NEW or owned by a live, unexpired acknowledgement'. The bound it enforces is read at line 231 from a row nothing in the repository has ever written.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: the loop line is the exact line the deadline lane named. Fires on a different instance: the predicate is structural (loop target vs derived population) and needs no knowledge of what any particular registry holds, so a future acknowledgement, waiver or exemption registry wired the same way is caught on the commit that adds it.
notes: Not a duplicate of any existing program. gate_is_wired_check.py answers 'does anything invoke this gate' and checker_execution_wiring_audit.py answers 'does anything but its own test invoke it'; both are satisfied here — this gate IS invoked, runs, and returns. The uncovered question is what its verdict was computed over.

title: declaration searched only inside a truncated window
docstring: A predicate deciding whether a required declaration is present must search the whole text. When the search runs over a fixed-size head or tail slice, an identical declaration reads as ABSENT purely because of where it sits, and the finding then names the wrong defect — it reports the author as having declared nothing. Declared outside the window and absent are different states and must stay different: the first is a formatting problem, the second is a governance one.
pattern: A required marker is looked for inside a fixed-size slice of a larger text, and a miss is reported as absence. The verdict then turns on a quantity nobody chose deliberately — the length of the prose above the marker, or the length of a path prefix ahead of it — so the same input flips verdict as unrelated text grows around it. The head-slice and the tail-slice shapes are one class: in both, a bound written to limit SIZE is silently doing the work of a predicate.
fix_action: For every slice of a text that feeds a marker search whose miss is reported as a finding: on a miss, re-run the same search over the full text. When the marker is found there, emit a distinct outcome naming the byte offset and the window size, never the absence outcome. Where the window exists to bound displayed output rather than to bound the search, keep it for display and widen the search to the whole text. Report as WARN any window whose search text can exceed it, so the class closes by construction instead of one instance at a time.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. CONTROL PAIR driven through the real predicate: two synthetic programs carrying a byte-identical declaration line, one at byte 26 and one at byte 5121. The 4000-byte head window returns 'blocking' for the first and None for the second — the same declaration, opposite verdicts, decided by the prose above it. Live population on that commit: 42 programs declare an enforcement intent, 42 are inside the window, 0 currently missed — so this rule adds no finding today and prevents the 43rd. The class DID occur: the wiring lane measured a twelve-line intent block at byte 8249 reported as 'declares no intent at all'. Second shape, independently measured by a different lane: a fixed-width TAIL window over run evidence, where the verdict flips between a 30-character and a 40-character scratch root and is stable at 20, 30 and at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 80. Denominator for the sweep: 44 head-slice sites of 100 characters or more across programs/*.py.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: the head-window site is one of the 44 and the re-search over full text recovers the byte-8249 declaration. Fires on a different instance: the predicate is about slice-then-search, not about which marker, so the tail-window evidence snippet measured by a second lane is caught by the same rule.

title: declared invocation accepted by its own parser
docstring: An invocation declared in a flow document is a contract with the invoked program's own argument parser. When the declared arguments omit something that parser marks required, the parser refuses before the check ever runs, and that refusal status collides with the status the flow reserves for input-not-applicable. The gate then scores as a pass on every input forever, and the failure points the wrong way: the worse the run, the more certainly it passes.
pattern: A declared invocation of a checking program is never validated against that program's own argument parser, and a parser refusal shares one exit status with a legitimate not-applicable skip. Any misdeclared invocation therefore lands in a passing tier with nothing examined. The class is systemic wherever a document declares invocations as text and an executor runs them without ever asking whether the program accepts them.
fix_action: Extend the existing invocability probe from the umbrella-registry population to the flow-document population, reusing the shared invocation helper so one definition of accepted survives. For each declared clause: resolve the program, resolve any subcommand the declared arguments select, and drive the parser alone with those arguments. Report a parser refusal as a declaration defect in its own tier and never fold it into not-applicable. Resolving subcommands is load-bearing, not a refinement: a static comparison against every required argument in the file reports a false positive on a program whose modes are subcommands, measured at exactly one such false positive over the declared population.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. 113 declared program-exit-status clauses extracted from the flow document. Static comparison of each declared argument vector against the required arguments of the named program yields 1 candidate, at step 4; driving that program's parser with the declared vector returns rc 1 with a content-earned refusal, so the candidate is a subcommand false positive and the live count is 0 of 113. The class DID occur and was measured by the matrix lane: a release-documents generator whose only declared invocation omitted two arguments its parser marks required, exiting 2, scored as a passing tier — and the same lane found a second instance of the identical shape among 24 findings. The sibling population is not clean: the umbrella-registry probe records 36 of 246 registered checkers rejecting the argument vector the umbrella builds.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: the omitted required arguments are exactly what a parser drive reports. Fires on a different instance: the predicate is per-clause and per-parser, so any future step declaring an invocation its program refuses is caught at declaration time rather than by a probe that runs only inside one test suite.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for the adjacent population: p0_gate_invocability_drift_check.py enforces exactly this shape over the umbrella registry, using the shared invocation helper, and records a non-invocable outcome as a VERDICT rather than a skip. What is missing is the population, not the predicate — the flow document's declared clauses are guarded only by a probe inside the matrix suite. This record is a population extension, not a new checker, and must be built that way.

title: invocation proved by parse not by text
docstring: Whether one module invokes another is a question about code, and a text search cannot answer it. About half of a large orchestrating module is prose, and a name that appears there is graded as a call, so the audit certifies wiring that does not exist. The consequence lands on the design: a step whose producer nothing dispatches reports a missing artefact for every input forever, and every reader charges that to the design rather than to the flow.
pattern: A wiring or consumption audit decides that one module invokes another by searching the caller's raw text. Prose naming the callee — a cross-reference in a docstring, a comment, a help string — counts as a call, so the audit's positive verdicts silently include every mention. The inverse holds too: a text scan cannot see a call assembled at run time, so both directions of such an audit are unsound and its clean verdicts carry no information.
fix_action: Parse the caller and decide invocation from the syntax tree: a call node, an element of an argument vector, or an import — never a docstring, a comment, or a help string. Where the caller builds an argument vector from a constant, resolve the constant. Report a name that occurs only in prose as its own outcome so the audit can state how many of its positive verdicts came from prose. Apply the same rule to consumption audits, where the question is whether a status is read rather than whether a name appears.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. flow_step_executor_coverage_check.py — whose docstring states that a step with no dispatching producer 'can only ever be MISSING, and that is the root cause of middle steps silently skipped' — contains no syntax-tree parse at all; it concatenates the runner sources and applies a regular expression. Corpus measured: 3,055,921 bytes of concatenated runner text, of which 1,472,929 bytes (48%) are docstring and comment. Confirming the consequence on the same commit: three producers declared by two path steps appear ZERO times in any runner, in code tokens or in string and comment tokens. A second lane measured the mirror image on the consumption side: of 7 runners, 5 name the compliance checker in prose only, and a text scan graded 3 of them as consumers of a verdict they never ask for.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: a parse of the runners returns no call node for the three producers, where the text scan returned a wired verdict. Fires on a different instance: the rule is about the method of proof, so it also catches the consumption-side scan a different lane hit, and any future audit that greps a caller for a callee's name.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for the adjacent population: hdl_declaration_scan_strips_comments_check.py enforces exactly this discipline for hardware-description declaration scans, and it is a live blocking gate. The program-invocation population has no equivalent, which is why the two audits above ship a text scan.

title: population pin without its member set
docstring: A pinned population count is invariant under any change that adds and removes the same number of members. An arrival and a departure landing in one batch leave the number identical, so the pin stays green while the population it names has become a different set, and a raw count read before and after tells the reader nothing. A count pin is a measurement only when the identities producing it are pinned beside it.
pattern: A test or a generated document pins the SIZE of a live population and never its MEMBERS. Compensating changes are invisible to it, and so is a restatement applied for a departure but not for the matching arrival — the pin can be arithmetically correct and still describe a different set. Where several pins over one population exist, the coarsest asserts first, so a finer pin that went stale in the same move is never reached.
fix_action: For every constant compared against a live re-derivation of a population size, require a member-identity pin in the same module, compared as a set in BOTH directions so a missing member and an extra member are named separately. Where pinning identities is impractical, require the count to be re-derived from the accessor at assertion time and refuse a hand-written literal. Refuse a membership assertion placed inside the branch that filters INTO the population, since that shape can only see a member arriving and never one leaving. Report each count-only pin together with the accessor it is compared against, so the population can be re-derived instead of argued about.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. POSITIVE CONTROL driven through the repository's own accessor: the live flow document yields 69 step ids; applying ONE departure and ONE arrival to a copy of it yields 69 again. The count pin is UNCHANGED; the member set changed, symmetric difference of exactly two ids. Census over the matrix test family on the same commit, counting only constants actually compared against a live re-derivation: 9 population pins, 0 member-set pins, so 9 of 9 are blind to a compensating change. The class DID occur, twice and in both directions: one lane found three coexisting populations for one grid (67, 68, and 68 in a published figure) against a live 69, with the delta measured as two arrivals and one departure and the pins 'restated for the departure only'; a second lane found a kind-by-kind pin stale in the same move as its own sum, with only the sum visible because it asserted first. A third instance is not drift at all — a pin that never matched the tree it was written against, proven by an empty diff of both its inputs between the authoring commit and the measurement.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: a member-set comparison names the two ids that moved, which the count could not. Fires on a different instance: the control shows the blindness is arithmetic, not specific to this population, so any pinned census over any live set is covered.

title: spawned gate whose status is discarded
docstring: A gate spawned as a subprocess delivers its verdict in its exit status. When the caller leaves the result unbound, turns off raise-on-failure, and encloses the call in a handler that swallows every exception, the verdict reaches nothing — and a comment beside the call can describe it as blocking with no reader noticing the contradiction. A call whose status no branch reads costs time and decides nothing.
pattern: A module spawns a checking program and discards the outcome: the result is unbound, the raise-on-failure flag is off, and the call sits inside a catch-everything block. The mirror shape is a gate whose declared subject is whether something RAN, implemented with no way to start a process or read a status at all. Both publish a verdict about something they never observed, and in both the prose around the code asserts the opposite.
fix_action: Parse every module that spawns a subprocess whose argument vector names a checking program. Refuse when the result is not bound to a name, when no branch reads its status, or when the call is enclosed by a handler catching every exception without re-raising. Refuse separately when a program whose name or docstring claims to check that something RAN contains no process-spawning call and no status read. Where a spawn is deliberately advisory, require that intent declared at the call site, so it is a decision on the record rather than an absence inferred from silence.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. INSTANCE 1 — phase3_one_shot_runner.py:40886: the comment above the call reads 'This direct, BLOCKING flow_compliance re-run ... so the orchestrator's headline can never lag its own sign-off'; the call passes the raise-on-failure flag as false, binds no result, and sits inside a handler catching every exception and continuing. Its exit status is consumed by nothing. INSTANCE 2 — full_suite_run_check.py, 294 lines, measured occurrences of subprocess 0, Popen 0, check-output 0, system 0, returncode 0, rc 0: a gate whose subject is whether the full suite RAN contains no way to start a run and no way to read one, and it decides by matching a command line as text. Both were found by different lanes on the same day, from different directions.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: a parse of the runner finds a spawn whose result is unbound inside a bare handler. Fires on a different instance: the second instance has no spawn at all and is caught by the mirror clause, which is why the rule carries both.

title: content pinned authority verified only at merge
docstring: A manifest that pins the content hash of authority files is rendered against one base and verified at one moment. A change that edits a pinned file is legitimate and expected, but between the edit and the re-render the manifest describes no tree that exists, and nothing on the editing side says so. A pin whose only reader runs after the point where it could still be repaired reports the breakage to the one person who cannot act on it.
pattern: A tracked manifest records content hashes for a set of protected paths and is consulted only by the merge-time tool. Every check that runs before merge is blind to a mismatch, so a branch that legitimately edits a pinned path carries an invisible obligation until a later tool refuses it. The verdict is correct and arrives at the wrong time, which is a different defect from a verdict that is wrong.
fix_action: Add a report-only check over the pinned path set: hash each path in the working tree, compare against the manifest, and name every mismatch together with the manifest identifier that must be re-rendered and the tool that renders it. Report rather than block — a mismatch on a branch that edits an authority path is the expected state, and blocking would refuse the very change the manifest exists to record. Run it wherever the repository-wide checks run, so the obligation is visible to the author instead of to the merge.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. The manifest pins 47 protected paths, with a content hash recorded for each in both the current and the next transition state. Readers on that commit: the merge-time verification script, the manifest author, the trusted-selection helper, the census tool, and two tests. The repository-wide hygiene script mentions it exactly once, and that occurrence is a COMMENT about which container image the manifest names — so no pre-merge check compares any pin against the tree. The wiring lane recorded the consequence in its own hand-off: it changed a file that is a pinned authority path, could not re-render the manifest because that artefact is owned by the lander, and wrote the obligation down precisely because nothing on its branch would report it.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: the edited authority path hashes differently from its pin and is named at edit time. Fires on a different instance: the check walks the pinned set, so any of the 47 paths edited by any branch is reported the same way.

title: reference control resolved through a mutable ref
docstring: A negative control must be built from a state that stays legitimately vulnerable. When the reference version is fetched by a branch name, the reference moves the moment the fix lands there, and the control begins asserting that a repaired program is still broken. The failure is silent in the direction that matters: the control stops discriminating and reads as a test that is merely wrong, rather than as coverage that has been withdrawn.
pattern: A test or a gate reads a reference version of a file, or derives the set of subjects it will cover, by resolving a mutable revision name instead of an immutable one. What the code covers then depends on where that name points at run time, so one tree yields different coverage in two clones and the difference surfaces as a changed collection count rather than as a defect. Only an immutable object name can hold a control's reference point still.
fix_action: Parse every test and gate for a process call that reads a revision. Refuse when the revision argument is branch-shaped — a remote-tracking name, a bare branch name, or an upstream shorthand — in any position a revision-reading subcommand consumes. Accept a working-tree pointer used against a fixture repository the caller has just created, because there the pointer is immutable in context: the discriminator is the branch shape, not the presence of a revision. Require a full object name and require the reason for choosing that object to be stated beside it.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. Syntax-tree census over every test and program: 31 process calls read a revision, of which exactly 1 resolves a branch-shaped name in a revision position — test_w4_absent_condition_is_not_a_pass.py:139, which loads its reference program version through a remote-tracking branch name. The other 30 read the working-tree pointer against a fixture repository the test itself just created, and are correctly not flagged. 1 finding, 0 false positives, and the finding is LIVE on that commit. Contrast with the naive form of the same search: a regular expression over the same corpus returns 15 sites across 12 files, 13 of them prose inside docstrings. The class was measured from a second direction by another lane: a guard whose subject set comes from a diff against the same branch-shaped name collected 116 cases in one clone and 12 in another, off the same tree.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: the reference read is the one site the census returns. Fires on a different instance: the same predicate catches the coverage-deriving diff a second lane hit, because both resolve a moving name where an immutable one is required.

title: denial that constitutes the value it appears to negate
docstring: A polarity guard that treats every denial as a negation inverts the sentences in which the denial IS the value. A specification saying that a quantity is not stated is granting freedom, not withholding a number, and an extractor whose subject is freedom must read that sentence as a positive. Applying a blanket denial check to such an extractor silently drops the freedoms the specification granted — the same disease as ignoring polarity altogether, pointing the other way.
pattern: An extractor reads English specification prose and either ignores denial polarity or applies it uniformly. Uniform application is wrong wherever the denial is constitutive of the extracted concept rather than a negation of it, so a correct guard needs two things: the span the denial governs, and a table separating constitutive idioms from negating ones. Adding the guard without the table converts a false negative into a false positive and reads as a fix.
fix_action: Give the shared polarity module a table of constitutive idioms keyed by the concept the calling extractor extracts, alongside its existing negating-denial patterns. Scope each denial to the value span with the module's existing scoping helper before classifying it. In the consultation gate, require every prose-reading extractor either to consult the module or to carry a declaration that its input is a grammar in which a denial cannot be spelled, and require that declaration to name its reason. Refuse a blanket denial check applied to an extractor whose extracted concept appears in the constitutive table.
measurement: origin/main e36d81c0a. The shared polarity module already ships the scoping helper and two denial pattern families, with two callers. A lane fixed 2 of 3 offending extractors this way — one now consults the module, one is declared not-prose with a stated reason that a port declaration is a grammar in which a negated declaration is unspellable — and MEASURED the third repair failing: adding the same blanket check to a line classifier broke 4 previously passing tests, because the fixture sentence granting freedom spells that freedom with a denial. The change was reverted and the finding left open rather than closed with a repair that inverts the sentences the function exists to read.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: the line classifier extracts freedom and would be refused a blanket denial check by the table clause. Fires on a different instance: the table is keyed by extracted concept, so any future prose extractor whose subject is an absence is decided by lookup rather than by whoever notices.
notes: ALREADY-PROGRAM for the consultation half: prose_polarity_consulted_check.py is a live gate demanding that a prose-reading extractor consult the shared module, and it is red on the shipped tree. The uncovered piece is narrower and is the reason it stays red — the module has no constitutive-versus-negating table, so the gate's own remedy cannot be applied to one of its three offenders.

title: wall clock bound standing in for a verdict
docstring: A forward-progress deadline of a second or less, applied to a subject that spawns processes, measures the host and not the code. Under load it fires and is reported as a defect in whatever change is in flight; on an idle host it passes and the same red is reported as fixed. A timing bound is a verdict only when the load it was measured under is recorded beside it, and a verdict taken from one sample on each side of a comparison is not a comparison.
pattern: A test kills its subject on a short wall-clock deadline and reports the kill as a substantive finding, with no record of the load the bound was measured under. The same identifier then reads green in one run and red in another off one tree, so a comparison between two arms attributes the difference to the change rather than to the machine — and the direction of that error is not random, because the arm run second inherits the load of the arm run first.
fix_action: Find every deadline literal below a stated floor that is compared against a wall clock in a test whose subject spawns a process. Require the verdict message to carry the load average and the elapsed time, and require the bound's own docstring to state the load it was chosen under. Refuse a deadline that is asserted as a substantive finding without those two numbers. Where a candidate red is used to compare two arms, require the arms to be interleaved rather than run in sequence, so neither inherits the other's load.
measurement: origin/main-based branch measurement by the ninth-dimension lane. One identifier appeared as a NEW red on the candidate arm and was not one: re-run in isolation, serially, on an idle host at load 2.9, it measured pass 0 fail 8 of 8 on the BASE tree and pass 0 fail 8 of 8 on the candidate — red on both, so the family run's green on the base was a FALSE GREEN. Its own diagnostic reads that the subject 'did not advance for > 0.45s — killed as hung, not slow'. The lane recorded that a single sample on each side would have filed it as damage the change had done. A second lane on the same day measured the mirror direction: 5 reds it first called parallel-execution artefacts, and 1 that was not.
original_and_class: Fires on the original: a 0.45 second forward-progress bound on a subject that spawns a two-way concurrent driver is below any defensible floor and carries no load in its message. Fires on a different instance: the predicate is the bound plus the subject, not the number, so any short deadline asserted as a finding is reported wherever it is added.

title: A landing's gate verdict is not recoverable from the repository
why_not_bucket_a: A deterministic rule can detect a missing attestation trailer, but there is no trailer to detect: the landing tool must first be changed to write its verdict into the commit, and every commit already on the branch needs a stated disposition before any rule can refuse anything. The exact input a program would see today is a commit message whose only evidence is a free-text sentence somebody chose to type, and no predicate over that text can distinguish a landing that ran the gates and passed from one that never started them.
pattern: The record that a landing ran its expensive checks lives outside the commit — in a local, untracked marker destroyed with the clone — so after the fact the only evidence is a sentence an author chose to type in the commit body. Whether any given landing was gated is not a question the repository can answer, and a run of landings that all skipped the gate is indistinguishable from a run that all passed it. The general shape is an enforcement whose attestation is not carried by the artefact the enforcement protects.
suggested_fix: Have the landing tool write its verdict as a commit trailer naming the gate set and the outcome, then add a check that every version-bearing commit carries one. Decide and record a single disposition for the commits that predate the trailer rather than exempting them silently. Two supporting items measured alongside it and cheap: the pre-push hook directory holds only sample files while a hook script ships in the tree, which reads as protection that is not installed — install it or delete it, since either state is honest and the current one is not; and the cheap half of a removed freshness gate re-derives its anchored figures in about one second and would have refused the commit that caused a whole family of failures, at the moment it was made.
session_context: Captured from a cluster of finished lanes covering the flow matrix, the gate wiring and the landing machinery. One lane measured 16 of 16 commits in a batch carrying a skip statement in the commit body, including one whose body also records that an earlier round had been refused for three new reds; the same lane measured that the local marker the landing tool writes does not exist in the clone and never enters a commit, so the question cannot be answered from the repository at all.
measurement: origin/main and the batch preceding it. 16 of 16 commits in one batch carry a landing-gate skip statement verbatim in the commit body. The commit that introduced the flow step behind a whole family of failures carries no gate statement of any kind. The local marker the landing tool writes is absent from the clone, and the hook directory contains only sample files with no override configured — so the bypass lane was never armed and a plain push would have enforced exactly as much as a forced one. A second lane independently found that a document-counter check catching a shipped file being clobbered has no caller outside a test suite the landing never runs.
